Parallel Analysis of Common-Factor Eigenvalues

Source: R/parallel_analysis.R
parallel_analysis.Rd

Compares factor-analytic eigenvalues with independently generated null references. Each correlation matrix is reduced by replacing its diagonal with the communalities of a fixed one-factor ML solution. The procedure concerns common factors, not principal components. The reference percentile is a null threshold; it is not a sampling confidence interval for an observed eigenvalue or a confidence statement about a factor count.

Usage

parallel_analysis(
  data = NULL,
  S = NULL,
  N = NULL,
  items = NULL,
  missing = "fiml",
  ordered = NULL,
  reference = "normal",
  B = 1000L,
  percentile = 0.95,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

data

Numeric raw observations, with items selecting columns. Supply exactly one of data or S.

S

Named positive definite covariance matrix, with N. Available only for a normal-reference analysis of continuous items.

N

Reference sample size for covariance input. For raw incomplete data it may be supplied as an explicit benchmark. With complete data the default is the number of cases; with FIML it is the complete-case count, and the output explicitly identifies this benchmark.

items

The items to analyze, by name: columns of data, or rows and columns of S, which is then reduced to them, in the order given; only the reduced matrix need be finite and positive definite. NULL, the default, analyzes every column of data or of S. Names that cannot be read as at least three distinct items are refused with an error of class dmar_items_invalid (see dmar_metadata).

missing

"fiml" (default), "ml", "listwise", or "pairwise". Continuous FIML obtains the unrestricted correlation matrix from cov_fiml. Ordered items follow the rule of fa_exploratory and factor_count: with no value missing, leaving missing out analyzes the items as they stand (listwise deletion with nothing to delete, recorded as "listwise"); with a value missing, the choice of "pairwise" or "listwise" is the user's, and leaving missing out is refused; giving "fiml" or "ml" for ordered items is refused whether or not a value is missing. Each refusal has class dmar_argument_invalid, as in those functions, and comes before anything is computed.

ordered

NULL, TRUE, or names of ordered items. The current ordered interface requires all analysis items to be ordered.

reference

"normal" (default) generates independent normal responses. With ordered items these are categorized using the observed univariate category probabilities, then polychoric correlations are estimated. "resample" samples each item's observed responses independently with replacement, preserving its empirical marginal distribution in expectation; ordered correlations remain polychoric.

B

Number of independent reference datasets, a single whole number, default 1000 (each one is generated and fit by a one-factor model). The fewest accepted depends on percentile: the reference quantile is reported only when at least 10 reference datasets lie beyond it and never from fewer than 100, which takes 200 at the default 95th percentile, 1000 at the 99th, and 100 at the 90th or at the median. A smaller B is refused before anything is computed (class dmar_count_invalid); see Details and dmar_bootstrap.

percentile

Null reference percentile, default 0.95.

conf_level

Confidence level for Monte Carlo uncertainty in the reference percentile, default 0.95. This is not observed-data sampling uncertainty.

seed

Optional seed, default NULL. A supplied seed restores the caller's random stream on exit.

Value

A dmar_tbl with ranks, observed estimate, reference_quantile, reference_mean, reference_quantile_ci_lower, reference_quantile_ci_upper (the Monte Carlo confidence limits for the reference quantile), and exceeds_reference. Attributes retain suggested_factors, reference_draws, counts, observed_boundary, method, and an explicit analysis_note, with the counts every result of the package that ran replications carries: B, B_used, n_dropped, B_required, and bootstrap_status (see dmar_bootstrap). Observed sampling confidence limits are unavailable and are not inferred from the null distribution.

Details

The fixed communality reduction is computed by stats::factanal() with its lower uniqueness bound of 0.005. Observed and null matrices use exactly the same reduction. Defined boundary solutions are retained and counted; failed fits are counted separately.

Reference datasets. The threshold of each rank is the percentile quantile of the eigenvalues of the B reference datasets, so it is located by the reference datasets that lie beyond it. The function runs only when B puts at least 10 of them beyond the quantile, and never with fewer than 100 (200 at the 95th percentile). A reference dataset whose fit fails is dropped and counted, never replaced. The count is held to the number requested. Thresholds and a factor count are reported only when no more than half of the attempted reference datasets failed; otherwise they are NA, the observed eigenvalues are returned, and the warning has class dmar_bootstrap_insufficient. When some failed and the thresholds were formed the warning has class dmar_bootstrap_replications_dropped. The result records B, B_used, n_dropped, B_required, and bootstrap_status as attributes beside the fuller counts list. options(dmar.bootstrap_exploratory = TRUE) lets a smaller B (2 or more) run for a first look or a demonstration; every such call gives a warning of class dmar_bootstrap_exploratory and the line under the table says so. These rules limit the error of drawing a finite number of reference datasets; they are not a coverage guarantee.

The suggested factor count is the number of consecutive ranks, starting at one, whose observed eigenvalues exceed their reference thresholds. It is evidence to combine with theory, model fit, and interpretability. Selection itself has no confidence interval here. Monte Carlo limits for the reference quantile use binomial order-statistic bounds; the quantile estimate uses R's type 7 interpolation. When reference fits fail, these quantities describe the null distribution conditional on returning a defined fit. Discarding failures can select a different distribution; the half-return rule does not repair that selection or establish the intended unconditional null quantile.

An incomplete-data FIML correlation matrix uses all observed values, whereas the complete-case reference size is only an explicitly labeled benchmark. It is not an effective sample size and is not guaranteed to be conservative. These references do not reproduce a study's missingness mechanism. They do not establish general MAR calibration. If fewer than three complete cases remain, choose a justified reference N explicitly rather than silently substituting the total sample size.

References

Horn, J. L. (1965). A rationale and test for the number of factors in factor analysis. Psychometrika, 30, 179–185. doi:10.1007/BF02289447

Author

Ken Kelley kkelley@nd.edu

Examples

set.seed(113)
items <- c("t1_visual_perception", "t2_cubes", "t4_lozenges",
           "t6_paragraph_comprehension", "t7_sentence", "t9_word_meaning")
# B = 200 is the fewest reference data sets the 95th percentile is
# reported from and keeps the example quick; the default is B = 1000.
parallel_analysis(holzinger_swineford, items = items, B = 200, seed = 113)
#>  term   rank estimate reference_quantile reference_mean
#>  rank_1 1    2.444    1.032              0.675         
#>  rank_2 2    0.568    0.170              0.122         
#>  rank_3 3    0.014    0.093              0.053         
#>  rank_4 4    -0.029   0.029              0.004         
#>  rank_5 5    -0.208   -0.019             -0.052        
#>  rank_6 6    -0.377   -0.074             -0.127        
#>  reference_quantile_ci_lower reference_quantile_ci_upper exceeds_reference
#>  1.031                       1.037                        TRUE            
#>  0.164                       0.208                        TRUE            
#>  0.083                       0.107                       FALSE            
#>  0.025                       0.039                       FALSE            
#>  -0.023                      -0.011                      FALSE            
#>  -0.085                      -0.063                      FALSE            
#> 
#> Common-factor parallel analysis: fixed one-factor ML communality reduction; normal reference; N = 301; 200 of 200 reference datasets usable. Reference percentile: 95%. Its Monte Carlo limits have nominal 95% coverage conditional on defined reference fits; discarded failures can select a different null distribution. They are not sampling CIs for the observed eigenvalues or the suggested factor count. Defined boundary reference fits: 92.
